{
  "root_cause": "The character count plugin removes the maxlength attribute from the container div ($module) instead of the textarea ($textarea), leaving the hard limit in place and truncating user input.",
  "repair_strategy": "Change the attribute removal target from $module to $textarea so the hard limit is lifted only on the input element, allowing the script to enforce limits via dynamic counting and messaging.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "src/govuk/components/character-count/character-count.js",
      "sha256": "b17688138faafe0e8e1b3b435f890c52c8dc6ca9fbcbb8644f2e93a5125f7b90",
      "before": "  // Remove hard limit if set\n  $module.removeAttribute('maxlength')",
      "after": "  // Remove hard limit if set\n  $textarea.removeAttribute('maxlength')"
    }
  ],
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Users can enter text beyond the limit and receive accurate visible and screen‑reader feedback about excess characters, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (keyboard), 2.4.3 (focus order), and 4.1.2 (name, role, value).",
  "functional_risks": [
    "If other code mistakenly expects the maxlength attribute to be removed from the container, removing it from the textarea instead could leave the attribute on the container (harmless).",
    "The change does not affect the fallback maxlength for users without JavaScript, which remains on the textarea."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Type more than 30 characters into the summary field and verify the full text is retained.",
    "Verify the textarea receives the govuk-textarea--error class and the visible counter shows a negative remaining count.",
    "Confirm the screen‑reader live region announces the excess count.",
    "Ensure form submission includes the complete text.",
    "Confirm that with JavaScript disabled, the maxlength attribute still prevents entry beyond 30 characters."
  ]
}

Indeed they try to remove maxlength attribute from the module (the div), but the maxlength attribute is on the textarea, not the div. So the hard limit remains, causing truncation.

Root cause: The character count plugin incorrectly removes the maxlength attribute from the container div instead of the textarea, leaving the hard limit in place and truncating input.

Repair strategy: Change the removal target from $module to $textarea.

Edits: one edit for the JS file.

Expected accessibility effect: Users can type beyond limit and receive appropriate error messaging via visible and screen‑reader character count, meeting WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard, 2.4.3 focus order, 4.1.2 name/role/value.

Functional risks: Potential regression if other code relies on maxlength attribute being removed from container; but unlikely. Might affect fallback for non‑JS users (they still have maxlength). Ensure no side effects.
